page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes dedicated CPU allocation with hyper-threading enabled, providing two threads per core. The processor is equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI.

The instance is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes 2458 GB of local NVMe storage and supports Premium Storage options. No dedicated GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ds_v4 demonstrates strong performance in memory bandwidth, achieving 207.3 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 95.23 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Passmark database operations are also strong at 22,567.01. However, CPU-bound tasks such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance fall within the average range. Large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B parameter model yielding a poor result of 2.33 tokens/sec due to the absence of hardware acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D64ds_v4 offers a balanced resource profile for workloads requiring substantial local storage and memory bandwidth without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. It is suitable for relational databases, enterprise applications, static web serving, and software compilation.
